# Problem Review: ${problem_category} tickets miss SLA because they can't be resolved at first line

**Scope:** ${overall_tickets} incidents opened ${overall_window_label} (ServiceNow event log, UCI dataset 498). **Author:** Operations analysis. **Status:** for review.

## 1. Problem statement

**${problem_category} is the largest single source of SLA breaches on the desk.** It makes up ${problem_share}% of tickets (the #${problem_volume_rank} category by volume) but ${problem_breach_share}% of all SLA breaches. Half of its tickets breach (${problem_breach_rate}%, against ${problem_breach_rate_rest}% for every other category). The median ticket takes ${problem_median_h} hours to resolve, against ${problem_median_h_rest} hours elsewhere. Only ${problem_first_line_share}% of these tickets are resolved by the first-line desk, compared with ${problem_first_line_share_rest}% for the rest of the workload.

## 4. Root cause analysis (5 whys)

| Why? | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Why does ${problem_category} drive the most breaches? | Its tickets take far longer to resolve (median ${problem_median_h} h against ${problem_median_h_rest} h). | **Data** |
| 2. Why do they take longer? | Only ${problem_first_line_share}% are fixed at first line. The rest wait in a second-line queue, where the median is ${problem_other_groups_med_h} h. | **Data** |
| 3. Why can't first line fix them? | There's no documented fix for first line to use: knowledge is attached on ${problem_knowledge_rate}% of tickets, half the desk rate. Intake also misses information, so a third of tickets stall in "Awaiting User Info". | **Data** (rates). The claim that no first-line procedure exists is an **assumption**, to be confirmed with the desk lead. |
| 4. Why is there no documented fix or clear route? | Ownership is spread over ${problem_resolver_groups} resolver groups, with a ${fastest_l2_median_h} h median in the fastest (${fastest_l2_group}) and ${slowest_l2_median_h} h in the slowest (${slowest_l2_group}). Nobody owns the category end to end. | **Data** (spread). That this causes the missing knowledge is an **assumption**. |
| 5. Why has nobody owned it? | The faults recur (problem records are linked ${problem_problem_link_rate}% of the time against ${problem_problem_link_rate_rest}% elsewhere), but the other tickets are still handled one at a time instead of being fixed at the source. | **Data** (link rates). That problem management isn't driving a permanent fix for this category is an **assumption**. |

**Root cause (working hypothesis):** ${problem_category} has no owning team and no first-line resolution path, so tickets that first line could solve are queued in slow second-line teams.

**What the data can't tell us** (because labels are anonymised and there's no free text): what the category actually is, or whether its fixes need access rights that first line doesn't have. Confirm both with the desk before committing to the long-term fixes.

## 5. Recommended fixes

**Quick wins (2–4 weeks)**
1. Write a first-line knowledge article for the top subcategory (${problem_top_subcategory}, ${problem_top_subcategory_share}% of the category) and attach it in the ticket template.
2. Add mandatory intake questions for ${problem_category} (see the runbook) to cut "Awaiting User Info" stalls.
3. Route by rule: send ${problem_category} tickets that first line can't solve to the fastest-performing group (${fastest_l2_group}) instead of a free choice of ${problem_resolver_groups} groups.

**Long-term (1–2 quarters)**
1. Name one owning group for ${problem_category}, with a monthly review of its SLA and its first-line resolution rate.
2. Open a problem record for the top recurring subcategories and fix the underlying fault, not each ticket.
3. Give first line the access or tools it needs for the common fixes (confirm what's needed first).

## 6. Expected impact

| Scenario | Change | Customer wait hours saved per month | Breaches avoided per month | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **A (primary)** | First-line resolution of ${problem_category} goes from ${problem_first_line_share}% to the desk rate of ${problem_scenario_fl_target_share}% (≈${problem_scenario_fl_tickets_shifted_pm} more tickets a month fixed at first line) | ≈${problem_scenario_fl_hours_saved_pm} | ≈${problem_scenario_fl_breaches_avoided_pm} | Category breach rate ${problem_breach_rate}% → ${problem_scenario_fl_new_cat_breach_rate}%. Desk SLA ${overall_sla_pct}% → ${problem_scenario_fl_new_overall_sla}% |
| B | Halve the number of reassigned ${problem_category} tickets (≈${problem_reassigned_pm} a month today) | ≈${problem_proj_hours_saved_pm} | ≈${problem_proj_breaches_avoided_pm} | Category breach rate → ${problem_proj_cat_breach_rate}% |

The scenarios overlap, so don't add them together. **How the estimates are built:** each ticket that moves is assumed to take the median time and breach rate of the group it moves to. That's a correlation, not a controlled test, because first line may already keep the easier tickets. Treat the figures as an upper bound and check them against the measures below.

## 7. How success will be measured

The targets apply scenario A's relative improvement to the latest month (${latest_label}).

| Measure | Whole window | ${latest_label} (baseline) | Target | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| ${problem_category} first-line resolution % | ${problem_first_line_share}% | ${latest_problem_first_line_share}% | ≥ ${problem_scenario_fl_target_share}% | Power BI, Problem Review page |
| ${problem_category} breach rate | ${problem_breach_rate}% | ${latest_problem_breach_rate}% | ≤ ${latest_target_problem_breach_rate}% | Power BI / Excel Top 10 |
| Share of ${problem_category} tickets that went to "Awaiting User Info" | ${problem_awaiting_user_rate}% | — | ≤ ${problem_awaiting_user_rate_rest}% (desk rate) | Event log |
| Knowledge attached on ${problem_category} tickets | ${problem_knowledge_rate}% | — | ≥ ${problem_knowledge_rate_rest}% (desk rate) | Event log |
| Desk SLA met % | ${overall_sla_pct}% | ${latest_desk_sla_pct}% | ≥ ${latest_target_desk_sla_pct}% | Excel Summary |

Review monthly for three months. If first-line resolution rises but the breach rate doesn't fall, the bottleneck is second line, so move to the long-term fixes.
